Tech Report: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • In a recent development, last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

In a recent development, last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully debuted on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Industry observers note that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Industry observers note that “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” claims Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

It has been revealed that more than 10 years in the making, MMX debuted on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

According to recent reports, MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to blueprint, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” claims Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

Sources indicate that the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Sources indicate that before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

In a recent development, it will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation demonstrates how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

It has been revealed that once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” states Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday states.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Industry observers note that idefix’s interactions with its upcoming home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec states. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

It has been revealed that what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel notes the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Recent findings suggest that once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel claims. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Industry observers note that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this glitch and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu indicates.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Sources indicate that once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

According to recent reports, “We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel claims. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

According to recent reports, “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu claims. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The presenter mentioned he declined the opportunity to return to the motoring show he helped turn into a global phenomenon alongside Jeremy Clarkson and James May.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Richard Hammond has revealed that the BBC sounded him out about getting back behind the Top Gear wheel for the show’s upcoming reboot.

The presenter mentioned he declined the opportunity to return to the motoring show he helped turn into a global phenomenon alongside Jeremy Clarkson and James May.

Hammond disclosed the BBC’s approach during an interview with Times Radio on the day that Gordon Ramsay was unveiled as the new host of Top Gear.

In a recent development, “I did talk to them about Top Gear relaunching, and I’m sure they went to the others as well. They came to me, and [asked] was I interested? ‘No, I’m too old,’ [I responded],” Hammond mentioned. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Gordon Ramsay To Host Revived 'Top Gear' For BBC News BBC Journalists Vote To Take Strike Action Over Job Cuts.

Industry observers note that “I’ve done it. I wouldn’t want to revisit it. That was our Top Gear, wasn’t it? We did it, the three of us, and when we left and went on together, it was the three of us. But that was our show.

“The BBC owns Top Gear and has had it for decades, and I think right now should be making a show that actually tells us what’s happening in the world of cars.”.

Times Radio presenter Kait Borsay asked Hammond if he would be interested if Clarkson and May returned to Top Gear.

“We’ve done it. Let somebody else. We made our show in the way we did, and for our time,” he replied. “The BBC should be making a TV show that tells us, the consumers: This is what’s happening in the world of transport.”.

Hammond hosted Top Gear between 2002 and 2015, before leaving the BBC with Clarkson and May and launching The Grand Tour on Amazon Prime Video.

Ramsay was announced as the next host of Top Gear four years after Andrew Flintoff’s crash. Ramsay will lead the series alongside a soon-to-be-announced lineup of co-presenters, with The Stig returning.

Filming will take place across the UK and around the world in 2027, with the Top Gear test track at Dunsfold Aerodrome in Surrey once again serving as the show’s home.

Ramsay remarked: “At its very best Top Gear has always been about the unexpected – surprising, entertaining and just the right amount of chaos. That’s the spirit we want to build on, bringing a fresh energy and ambition to create something truly thrilling for a whole newly introduced generation of audiences.”.

Tech Report: Lincoln’s Thanksgiving Lesson For Us Now: Don’t Claim Victory Yet

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that one hundred sixty-three years ago, Americans gathered for what began an unbroken annual tradition: Thanksgiving.
  • It has been revealed that some Americans will come to the table this year carrying wounds of their own.
  • It has been revealed that some observers have called this month’s midterms a “Gettysburg moment.” The comparison is apt, but not for the reason most people think.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one hundred sixty-three years ago, Americans gathered for what began an unbroken annual tradition: Thanksgiving. It came one week after Abraham Lincoln stood in a field at Gettysburg to dedicate a cemetery. In three days of fighting there that July, 50,000 Americans had been killed, wounded, captured, or gone missing. That summer, after Gettysburg and Vicksburg, Lincoln had called for a day of thanksgiving for the Union’s victories. By fall, he asked for something more. He did not ask a grieving country to set its losses aside. He asked it to give thanks despite the losses, to remember the “widows, orphans, mourners, or sufferers,” and to work to “heal the wounds of the nation.”.

It has been revealed that some Americans will come to the table this year carrying wounds of their own. And amid a common narrative that Americans are hopelessly divided, many may feel a bit lighter because the nation came together to hold free and fair elections this month. Still, many will sit across the table from people who view the results differently.

It has been revealed that some observers have called this month’s midterms a “Gettysburg moment.” The comparison is apt, but not for the reason most people think. Gettysburg was not a turning point on July 3, 1863, when the guns went quiet. It became one in the hard months that followed, because of what ordinary people did next.

Recent findings suggest that when Lincoln delivered his address at Gettysburg that November, he didn’t take credit. He didn’t use the moment as an opportunity to win a factional political debate. Instead, he reminded the country of its core values and focused on the unfinished work ahead. Lincoln gave us a lesson for our times about what to do with a moment of reckoning. He came to dedicate a cemetery, and instead of taking a victory lap, he used his brief address to look ahead:.

In a recent development, “It is for us the living . . . to be dedicated here to the unfinished work which they who fought here have thus far so nobly advanced.”.

With those words, Lincoln passed the work to the people.

According to recent reports, the hardest fighting was still ahead. When Lincoln came to Gettysburg, the war’s outcome was far from settled, and Gettysburg had not yet acquired its reputation as the turning point. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

It became one because of what those still living did next. In the months after Gettysburg, the South didn’t simply give up just because their defeat seemed inevitable. Instead, it dug in, fighting harder to make victory for the Union as costly as possible. But, Union soldiers kept fighting in a series of battles — some of the bloodiest of the war — slowly but steadfastly liberating parts of the South from enslavement. By 1865, the grim work paid off and the Union had prevailed.

In 2026, we are standing now where the crowd stood when Lincoln came to Gettysburg: after the battle, before anyone knows how the war ends and with grueling work ahead.

In a recent development, in 2021, after January 6, the United States was first added to a global list of “backsliding” democracies. The slide has since sharply accelerated. Trump has pardoned the people who stormed the Capitol, sent troops into American cities, sought to suppress the right to vote, and went to war with Iran without Congress.

According to recent reports, but as a Republican-controlled Congress abandoned its constitutional duty to check the president, and powerful law firms, universities, and media companies capitulated, ordinary people stepped forward. Residents filled the streets to protect neighbors from armed federal agents. Millions joined “No Kings” marches in all 50 states. People and state attorneys general filed more than 900 lawsuits and won orders protecting people’s rights.

Earlier this month, despite threats from the White House and its allies, Americans voted. Roughly 49 percent of eligible voters cast ballots, the second-highest midterm turnout since 1914. Power shifted in Texas. Mississippi elected its first Black senator since Reconstruction. Kansas sent a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in 94 years. Related Content Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed For Weather The Man Who Broke the Texas Democratic Party to Save It Stephen Miller Wants to Win Back Young Men. It Might Not Be So Easy ‘Dare Him to Veto It’: Democrats Are Ready to Push for Real Reform.

Since the election, the political conversation has fixated on what new Democratic majorities should do with their power, who might run in 2028, and whether the Republican Party will reform itself. These are crucial questions, but some of this discourse falls back into a habit the media and political classes must break: It treats Americans as spectators. This election was won by people who would not sit on the sidelines: voters who demonstrated up despite threats, neighbors who organized, Americans who refused to accept that the outcome was already decided. The most important question now is not what political parties will do, it is what we, the people, do next.

Recent findings suggest that democracy is not decided on Election Day. It is built between elections — by people, not parties — in communities, courtrooms, statehouses, and school boards. And the gains voters made at the polls can be taken apart there, too, quietly, while no one is watching.

We are already seeing this. In Texas, outgoing officeholders have met behind closed doors to discuss stripping power from the lieutenant governor voters just chose. U.S. Senate Republicans are racing to confirm lifetime judges before they lose their majority in January. And the president named Stephen Miller White House chief of staff days after the election, while his administration threatens members of Congress with criminal prosecution.

Industry observers note that no ballot will stop any of that. What can is what produced this month’s results: people who refused to look away — the plaintiff who signed a lawsuit, the neighbor on the sidewalk, the friend calling their lawmakers, the volunteer knocking doors.

We must pay attention after the cameras leave. Lame-duck sessions, rule changes, and quiet appointments are where hard-won results get undone. The threats from the executive branch will continue through 2028, and the lawsuits and movements that held the line will be needed more, not less.

Sources indicate that we must stay focused. Americans want a government that delivers — costs they can afford, healthcare, safe air travel — and we should insist on it. We should also reject a false choice between accountability and a government that delivers. Values-based accountability is not retribution. It is how a democracy indicates that no one is above the law, and it is part of delivering for people. We also should stay focused on longer-term changes that the nation and the people need to avoid a backslide in the future. Even if bolder changes like the U.S Supreme Court or passing comprehensive voter reform won’t get past this president’s veto, the next two years are the time to build the case for them. The people should not let political gridlock curtail their demands for a changed future. Trending Stories Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65 U2 Perform Dolly Parton's Final Recording During NFL Halftime Show Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Was the Wildest of the Wild Boys The Country Song About Losing Your Virginity That Became an Enduring Hit.

According to recent reports, we must build community. This fall, voters rejected culture wars and runaway oligarchs. Elon Musk alone spent an estimated $474 million to elect Republicans. In Texas, Republicans poured at least $78 million into anti-trans ads against Senator-elect James Talarico, nearly half of the GOP’s ad spending in the race. Texas flipped anyway. Voters showed they could see past division, and that they weren’t for sale. We should expect attempts to divide us to accelerate. The ties we build across differences are the infrastructure of self-government, and they hold only if we keep using and building them.

Sources indicate that gratitude and grief are two sides of the same coin. Lincoln understood that, and he asked a wounded nation to hold both. This Thanksgiving, they call us to the same thing: to find the grit and grace to keep going, and to make the fighting chance the midterms gave the people our nation’s watershed moment. Some 15,000 were in the crowd at Gettysburg. Lincoln wasn’t speaking only to his generals, his Cabinet or Congress. He was speaking to the people. The work was theirs. Now it is ours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

It has been revealed that iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

Opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

Sources indicate that you can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point people toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Recent findings suggest that apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the upcoming Siri experience.

The last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

According to recent reports, now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

According to recent reports, I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

In a recent development, apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

Recent findings suggest that after 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s upcoming Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

Industry observers note that after months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

What do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

It’s a Thanksgiving Day tradition to gather the family around the TV to watch the best athletes in America contend for glory — we’re, of course, referring to the dogs of the National Dog Show, which sees two hours of canine competition across seven groups.

The National Dog Show has historically followed the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. This year will look a little different, as the Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed to Saturday, Nov. 28 due to severe weather. This marks the first time the parade has ever been postponed, although it was cancelled for several years during World War II. The National Dog Show, which was pre-taped earlier this month at the Greater Philadelphia Expo Center, is still scheduled to air as planned.

The show will air at noon, local time, on NBC and will be preceded by a replay of last year’s parade. Last year’s Best in Show was Soleil, a Belgian sheepdog, who is looking to defend her title this year. The dog breeds are split into seven groups: herding, hound, non-sporting, sporting, terrier, toy, and working.

The competition is presented by the Kennel Club of Philadelphia and sponsored by Purina, and the broadcast will be hosted by John O’Hurley and David Frei, who are returning for their 25th year.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking to watch the National Dog Show, you can catch it on NBC. If you don’t have cable or an antenna, you can stream it by subscribing to Peacock, or by getting a free trial to a live-TV streaming service like DirecTV or Fubo. Here are a few options.

DirecTV is one of the best live-TV streaming services thanks to its broad selection. You can get NBC a variety of packages, all of which come with a five-day trial.

It has been revealed that fubo carries NBC in both of its tiers and is a particularly popular streaming service with sports fans. Like DirecTV, you can get a five-day free trial. You also get a discount on the first month after the trial.

Hulu + Live TV has a shorter three-day free trial, and it includes NBC in its main initiative. The service costs $99.99 a month once the trial ends.

In a recent development, electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then indicates how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

iOS 27 brought several upcoming features to the Messages app, including a setting that’s long been a popular request: the ability to customize or turn off the audio button. Here’s how to use it.

With iOS 27, Apple fixed a lot of bugs and also granted many feature requests from over the years.

Recent findings suggest that siri AI is the biggest example of that, offering a substantial upgrade over the old Siri. But smaller changes in apps like Calendar, Mail, and Messages reflect this focus on wish fulfillment.

In Messages, there’s a fresh setting that I instantly starting using. It lets you turn off the audio button that normally lives on the right side of the text input field.

The audio button has been conveniently accessible there for years, but I never use it. I don’t think I’ve ever sent an audio message. Sometimes I use dictation, but that’s always available from the bottom-right of the keyboard.

It has been revealed that since I never need that button, the only time it gets pressed is by accident. And as I suspect a lot of users have encountered—including Justin Bieber—it’s very easy to hit by accident.

In a recent development, thankfully, iOS 27 has the fix. To disable the audio button, follow these steps:.

Even if you turn the audio button off, you can still send audio messages by hitting the + button to open your iMessage apps then selecting ‘Audio.’.

Sources indicate that if you prefer to keep the button active, you can alternately now select ‘Record Audio’ or ‘Start Dictation’ as its function. That way the button will always stay set to your preference instead of dynamically changing like it did before.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s the Thanksgiving season, which means the turkey is in the oven, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade is on the screen, the pies are cooling on the countertop, and that box of Christmas lights you wadded up into a ball last year is waiting for you just around the corner.

Sources indicate that while the holiday season mainly involves eating your bodyweight in dishes made primarily of butter, it’s also about giving thanks. And what better way to revel in the nostalgia of family gatherings than rewatching some of the most memorable Thanksgiving tables to ever grace television screens?

From tense discussions about family fortunes and hijinks-heavy parent traps to just so many extra turkeys, here are 11 of the best Thanksgiving-themed episodes of TV.

In a recent development, throughout Fresh Girl’s seven seasons, the gang share multiple Thanksgiving dinners — almost all of which immediately devolve into chaos. But there’s something infinitely rewatchable about “Parents,” where Jessica Day (Zoey Deschanel) attempts to get her divorced parents back together over the pumpkin pie. It’s a masterclass of character work from the late Rob Reiner and Jamie Lee Curtis  — who play Jess’s parents — and Curtis’ attempt to seduce Jessica’s crush Nick (Jake Johnson) with a turkey baster can’t be touched.

Sometimes life is good as a teenage Upper East Side socialite destined for Yale and the sweet life. And then sometimes, you’re Blair Waldorf (Leighton Meester) and you spend all day trying to perfect your family’s traditional pumpkin pie only for your father to bail on the dinner he promised he was coming to. At least your best friend is having a good time. Except, oh wait — all the way in Dumbo, Serena van der Woodsen (Blake Lively) finds out that her mother and her latest boyfriend’s dad have spent decades pining after each other. With its sepia-toned flashbacks and classic 2000s pop hits, “Blair Waldorf Must Pie” defines the aesthetic of Gossip Girl and sets up Meester for a career-defining exercise in fleeting emotional openness.

Thanksgiving is famously a holiday that’s celebrated by overeating. But Gilmore Girls takes it to a hysterical level in “A Deep-Fried Korean Thanksgiving.” Lorelai (Lauren Graham) and Rory (Alexis Bledel) cherish the amount of friendship and love in their life. But when all of their friends want them to attend separate Thanksgiving dinners, they choose the worst of all the options and decide to attend all of them rather than let anyone down. The side-plot of Lane (Keiko Agena) and Dave Rygalski’s (Adam Brody) budding love and first kiss is a heartwarming addition to the madcap food marathon, which pushes the titular girls’ stomachs and secrets to the limit.

Sources indicate that this Grey’s Anatomy Thanksgiving episode reveals everyone’s favorite medical residents pushed to their breaking points when their social lives crash into their professional goals. Yes, it’s especially memorable to watch the often-bullied George O’Malley (T.R. Knight) finally find common ground with his camo-wearing, gun toting family. But the crux of this episode is the gastronomic stylings of Dr. Burke (Isaiah Washington) and Izzie Stevens (Katherine Heigl), who treat their prepped kitchen like an O.R. — turning their Thanksgiving feast into a lesson in surgery.

Family means quality time. It also means knowing when not to have faith in your relatives. When Phil (Ty Burrell) takes over turkey duty for Thanksgiving, his wife Claire (Julie Bowen) makes a secret backup. But when an electric problem forces them to decamp to her father’s house, Jay (Ed O’Neill) and Gloria (Sofia Vergara) have to stay in their rooms or admit to the extended crew that they faked leaving on a  Thanksgiving cruise to avoid the drama of the holidays. It’s practically a carnival game with turkeys moving in and out of the oven, capped off with some truly comical voice work from cooking legend Nigella Lawson.

It might feel a bit blasphemous to not include the Bobs Burger episode that gave us Linda Belcher’s famous Thanksgiving-themed melody “Pass the cranberry sauce.” But in “Turkey In a Can,” Bob’s Burgers leaves the set dressing behind and tackles the real stressor behind Thanksgiving: sexual awakening. When Bob (H. Jon Benjamin) wakes up before Thanksgiving to find his brining turkey in the toilet, he has to keep making daily trips to the butcher to replace it. The butcher (Tuc Watkins) naturally thinks Bob is flirting — although he’s not usually into “sloppy bears,” as he puts it — but the return visits wear him down until Bob has to reject his advances. Not because he’s married, but because he’s “mostly straight.”.

Recent findings suggest that while press secretary CJ Cregg (Allison Janney) has to choose which of the turkeys wins a presidential pardon, President Josiah Bartlett (Martin Sheen) has to make an infinitely harder choice — deciding whether a boat of Chinese immigrants seeking religious refugee status will be allowed to stay in the country. Aaron Sorkin is a man of many words, but sometimes he pulls off an episodic feat that feels virtually impossible to emotionally recreate. It’s no wonder that “Shibboleth” — and its titular discussion about faith — remains one of the most beloved episodes in the entire series.

It has been revealed that you think your Thanksgiving dinner table gets a little tense? At least you’re not Tony Soprano (James Gandolfini), who’s trying to figure out how to keep his affair a secret, teach his teenager not to take ecstasy, and figure out whether or not to kill one of his henchmen in the same night — all while trying to ignore his sister’s new born-again boyfriend. Through its six seasons, The Sopranos takes care to show the immediate cost and unexpected struggles of running a mob empire — leaning heavy on moments of tense expecation. But “He Is Risen” takes the already comical moments in the mob series and slams them onto one crowded dinner table.

According to recent reports, yes, it’s a truth universally acknowledged that Ryan Murphy’s hit high school drama Glee completely jumped the shark once its main characters graduated and had to leave the halls of their beloved William McKinley High School. But the series’ relocation from Lima, Ohio to the streets of Upcoming York made even more magical celebrity run-ins become slightly more plausible. It’s a true gift that keeps on giving to be able to watch Sarah Jessica Parker, playing a Vogue editor, attend Rachel Berry and Kurt Hummel’s Bushwick-loft Thanksgiving. And once you watch her perform a mashup of “Let’s Have A Kiki / Turkey Lurkey Time,” this episode will become an annual must-watch.

Whenever you turn on an episode of Succession, you can pretty much be assured that Kendall Roy (Jeremy Strong) is having a no good, terrible, very bad day. But Succession’s Thanksgiving episode “I Went To The Market” does more than place Kendall’s long-suffering air front and center. It uses the Thanksgiving holiday to prove just how unsuited the entire family is being normal. While Kendall preparing a vote of no-confidence is the crux of the episode, much of the humor coalesces around Cousin Greg (Nicholas Braun)’s trip driving his grandfather Ewan (James Cromwell) — Logan’s brother — down from Canada. In addition to the signature Tom Wambsgans quips — “Canada, with the healthcare and the ennui?” — Tom (Matthew Macfadyen) has to figure out his prenup with Shiv and how to destroy records of the Brightstar Cruise Lines crimes at the same time. It’s classic Succession — no one gets turkey before a little corporate espionage.

Recent findings suggest that I don’t care if there’s an episode where Monica (Courtney Cox) actually puts a turkey on her head — the one  with Brad Pitt as a secret guest star remains an ideal Friends scenario. In “The One with the Rumor,” Pitt stars as Will Colbert, Monica’s high school friend who shows up to Thanksgiving unrecognizable after losing over 150 pounds. “It’s no fat, no sugar, no dairy,” Pitt notes, handing Monica a pie. “It’s no good, throw it out.” His arrival was a surprise to the live studio audience, who shriek in delight at his appearance. (Pitt was married to Friends cast member Jennifer Aniston at the time.) Watching the cast fight over the barbs they traded in high school means a flurry of jokes, but it’s the delighted screams and cheers behind the camera that sell this episode.

  • This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight.
  • Industry observers note that that price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” patch to the Vertix 2 and 2S. Coros notes it pairs the brand's brightest display yet with long battery life, and after unboxing it myself, I can definitely say it has a more refined feel that could indeed suit the office as well as the summit.

This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight. The Vertix 4 will be available to buy starting on Black Friday, Nov. 27, but it won't exactly be at a discount: It costs $799, a $100 increase over the Vertix 2S.

Industry observers note that that price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is at the moment on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

I've only just started testing the Vertix 4 and haven't even had enough time to get through its substantial battery life, but I can share some first impressions, particularly in how it compares with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro that launched earlier this year.

Industry observers note that built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

Previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

Coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:.

Recent findings suggest that music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

Industry observers note that on paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.
  • Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

Industry observers note that the iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

Sources indicate that the iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

The iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

For most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

Football Practice and Red Dirt Music: On the Field With Oklahoma Band Keyland

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that over the next few months, Ross will attempt to strike a rather unique balance as coach and touring artist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there is arguably no better day for football — watching it or playing it — than the autumnal crispness of Thanksgiving. But on this particular late summer afternoon, despite triple-digit temperatures and the Oklahoma sun making it feel even hotter, football is the sweat-drenched task at hand: Coach Kyle Ross is putting me through practice. It’s not lost on either of us that Ross’s primary job is coaching high-energy junior-high athletes in the state’s flagship football program, at Bixby, and I’m an out-of-shape journalist in his late 40s. If I finish Ross’s drills upright and healthy, we’ll declare it a success.

“What are you? Three-for-three or four-for-four catching passes here?” Ross — who is also the founder and frontman of the band Keyland — asks me. My football career ended in high school, 30 years ago, but I was a slot receiver with a reputation for catching anything thrown my way. What would my parents say if I started dropping passes now? “I will throw my body on this turf to not miss a pass,” I promise him.

Recent findings suggest that over the next few months, Ross will attempt to strike a rather unique balance as coach and touring artist. He’ll headline and sell out the Mercury Lounge in Tulsa, 30 minutes north of Bixby, open an East Coast run for Morgan Wade, and announce a series of 2027 dates supporting Kaitlin Butts. And while he’s ostensibly promoting Knuckle Sandwich, Keyland’s third studio album, Ross will always have football season in the back of his mind.

“I haven’t found anything better to do,” Ross claims of why he continues to coach. “Except for maybe, get paid to play guitar and drink beer.”.

Few pastimes are as all-encompassing in Oklahoma as football. Its two largest college programs — Oklahoma and Oklahoma State — play their home games in modern stadiums to sold-out crowds on most Saturdays in the fall, but it’s the high-school version of the sport that unites the state. Students, fans, and parents fill stadiums in the state’s urban cores and rural farm towns every Friday night, and for the past decade, no program has dominated this landscape like Bixby’s. The varsity Spartans are eight-time defending champions in Oklahoma’s largest class and this season were ranked No. 1 again by the state’s largest media outlet. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Recent findings suggest that this is Ross’s program. He’s an assistant coach for Bixby’s eighth-grade team and a junior-high English teacher. He grew up in rural Missouri, playing football through high school. Shortly after graduating college, Ross befriended Tyler Schneider — Bixby’s longtime offensive coordinator. The two hit it off, and within weeks, Ross joined the Spartan’s staff. Seven years later, Ross is throwing passes to me on the same turf that those Spartans play their home games. We’re here to talk about music, but I am here to experience what it’s like being one of Ross’s players.

“Let’s go!” he shouts as I haul in another pass. “And he scores!”.

In a recent development, as it happens, that particular end zone is where I scored my last touchdown as a player. Before Bixby became the state’s juggernaut program, it was a mid-sized school in the same conference as my hometown team, the Okmulgee Bulldogs.

Sources indicate that when he’s playing as Keyland — Ross uses the moniker interchangeably for his solo and full-band demonstrates, named for a duck club he and his father used to hunt near his Chillicothe, Missouri, hometown — he wears an infectious smile that’s integral to his show. He describes the irreverent Knuckle Sandwich, which Keyland recorded at the Sonic Ranch studio outside of El Paso, as a product of pals hanging around for several days and finding music at the end of it. Related Content Jason Scott and the High Heat Are the Cool, If Raunchy, Band Americana Music Needs Honky-Tonk Woman: Kaitlin Butts Is As Ambitious As She Wants to Be You’ve Been Streaming ‘Broken Window Serenade.’ This Is the Texas Band Who Wrote It Wade Bowen Is Texas Music.

“This album is about taking what you do seriously, but not taking yourself seriously,” Ross states. “That kind of embodies the whole creative process in recording it. It’s more of a hang than anything, and we get music at the end of it.”.

According to recent reports, it’s a microcosm for his entire music career. He had a guitar growing up, but played it sparingly. It was not until he was in college and caught a Chris Stapleton gig that he decided to give music a try. “I fell in love with Chris Stapleton, and that was the entry way to the long rabbit hole I fell into,” he says.

According to recent reports, landing a full-time job right in the heart of Tulsa’s music community was a bout of good fortune. Ross befriended Brandon Clark, frontman of the Red Dirt outfit BC & the Major Rig and highly respected in Red Dirt circles. Clark has a weekly gig at Mercury Lounge, and in 2022, he suggested that Keyland get booked at the bar.

Keyland’s first Mercury Lounge show was opening for the Big Rig. Shortly afterward, venue general manager Ashley Kirkley booked Keyland as a headliner. The show sold out, and Keyland have been a regular since.

“Keyland is a great band, no doubt, but the energy and charisma that emanates from Kyle is palpable at every show,” Kirkley says. “Beyond being an incredible performer with a distinctive voice that is unlike anything I’ve heard, he is also one of the most down to earth, kindest people I have ever met. Kyle is always striving for greatness in everything he does. He’s an incredible human, and we are incredibly lucky to have him as a part of our music family.”.

Recent findings suggest that keyland have since gone on to, at least, regional notoriety. Ross has been booked multiple times at nearby Cain’s Ballroom, playing alongside the likes of Johnny Mullenax and opening a sold-out show for Josh Abbott earlier this year.

“Everyone’s at different levels of what they’re doing,” Ross claims of the Tulsa music community. “I have friends who have sold out a place like Cain’s. I’m friends with people who are doing house indicates for ten people. It almost seems like everyone has a very similar mindset of, ‘We’re almost there.’”.

Ross knows better than anyone that Keyland is growing at a fast clip. He is likely to come to a crossroads between coaching and making music before too many more gigs or summer practices pass. But until then, he’s happy to pull double duty. And even at Bixby, where the focus is annually on another state championship, he has found support. He had a fan from the start in Schneider, but he’s brought most of the Spartans’ coaching staff onto his bandwagon — and even a few players.

“There’s a huge Venn diagram of coaches’ interests outside of football, and one of them is music,” Ross says. “All the coaches are super supportive. We have over 20 coaches, and a huge number of them have been to more than one concert. It’s just a community-oriented place to work. The kids, as they get older, they start to appreciate it.”.

And on that note, practice is over. Ross’s actual players are starting to trickle in to Bixby’s behemoth of a training facility. Ross gives me a Bixby Spartans shirt for surviving his drills. Gérard Depardieu will stand trial in a criminal court on a rape charge related to accusations by actress Charlotte Arnould, after an appeal by his lawyers failed.

The Paris Court of Appeal remarked on Thursday that Depardieu would be tried for one part of the accusations levelled by Arnould against the actor.

The actress, whose father was an old friend of the actor, accuses Depardieu of raping and sexually assaulting her twice in his Paris mansion in the summer of 2018 after she went to him for acting advice. The court has ruled that Depardieu will be tried for the first alleged rape on August 7, 2018, but not the second alleged rape on August 13, due to insufficient evidence.

The decision to proceed with the trail comes eight months after Depardieu was found guilty of sexual assault and given an 18-month suspended sentence related to events on the set of Jean Becker’s The Green Shutters in 2021. Watch on Deadline.

The actor last week announced he was abandoning plans to appeal the sentence and issued a statement saying that he recognized his culpability and apologized for the hurt he had caused.

Just days after the letter was published, investigative newsite Mediapart published details of a fresh sexual assault and rape complaint against the actor related to events on the shoot of Guillaume Nicloux’s Thalasso in 2018.

His 18-month suspended sentence related to assaults on two female crew members on the set of The Green Shutters.

A number of women, who were not pressing charges, also gave evidence at the trial, including an actress who alleged Depardieu had shoved his hands into her knickers during a photo-call on the set of Netflix show Marseille.

Arnould was the first woman to pursue Depardieu in the courts in relation to sexual assault allegations, but her move came against a backdrop of growing rumors around the actor’s sexually inappropriate treatment of female extras and crew members on film sets.

Her complaint was initially dismissed by the courts following a nine-month investigation for lack of evidence, but she filed a second complaint as a civil party, which resulted in an investigating judge being appointed in 2020, and Depardieu being indicted for rape and sexual assault in 2021.

In between times, Depardieu’s public star plummeted following an exposé of his alleged sexual misconduct by state broadcaster channel France 2’s investigative show Complément d’Enquête, entitled “The fall of the ogre”, which aired in December 2023.

The allegations and 2026 guilty verdict have brought his acting career to a grinding halt. Since 2022, he has worked on only three productions, one of them directed by his longtime friend Fanny Ardant.

The criminal court is France’s highest level of court reserved for crimes carrying sentences of more than five years, if the accused is found guilty.

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Industry observers note that say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Industry observers note that swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The enhancement follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

#132348. Industry News: All the ‘GTA’ Games Ever, Ranked

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3285 w)
